purpose: Paroxetine is used to treat depression, anxiety disorders, panic attacks, obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). It can also help with social anxiety and certain mood-related symptoms of menopause. Your doctor may prescribe it for other conditions as well.
how_it_works: Your brain uses a chemical called serotonin to help regulate your mood and emotions. When serotonin levels are too low, it can lead to feelings of depression or anxiety. Paroxetine works by blocking the reabsorption of serotonin in your brain, allowing more of it to stay active and helping to improve your mood and reduce anxiety over time.
common_side_effects: Nausea, drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, sweating, constipation, or trouble sleeping are common, especially when you first start. Many of these improve after a few weeks. You may also notice changes in your sex drive or difficulty reaching orgasm.
warnings: Do not stop taking this medication suddenly without talking to your doctor, as this can cause withdrawal-like symptoms such as dizziness, irritability, or flu-like feelings. There is a small increased risk of suicidal thoughts in young people under 25, especially at the start of treatment — contact your doctor right away if this happens. Avoid alcohol while taking this medication. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as paroxetine may carry risks during pregnancy.
typical_dosing: Most adults start at 10 to 20 mg once daily, usually taken in the morning with or without food. Your doctor may gradually increase your dose based on how you respond, up to a maximum of 60 mg per day depending on the condition being treated. It can take 2 to 4 weeks before you start feeling the full benefit.
